_comment: THE PRODUCER SEAM'S MEMBER CENSUS AND ITS RULE TABLE. Data-Contract.md §5.
THIS FILE IS DATA FOR THE REASON `refusal-reasons.json` AND `snapshot-format.json` ARE:
two languages need it. `src/blocktracer/chain/contract_rules.nim` reads it with
`staticRead` at compile time — so a malformed table fails the BUILD — and
`tools/chain/snapshot-contract-selftest.mjs` reads it to check the reader against it.
It is §5's member census in machine-readable form: for every container the reader
opens, every member it consumes, whether the CONTRACT requires that member, and which
SUBSCRIPT the reader reaches it with. The two are different facts and conflating them
is what this whole deliverable exists to end:
required   what §5 says a producer must write
access     what `ingest.nim` does — `node["k"]` raises on absence, `node{"k"}` does not
A member that is OPTIONAL to the contract and reached by `[]` is a member the reader
crashes on and the spec says is fine. That is not a hypothetical: `provenance.l1ChainId`
was exactly that, §5.2 named none of the four provenance members the summary writer
reached, and the live follower's own mainnet output omitted it — so the producer this
repository ships wrote a snapshot the reader this repository ships raised `KeyError` on,
invisibly, because every committed fixture carried the member.
A member that is REQUIRED by the contract and reached by `{}` is legitimate exactly when
some rule enforces it by name instead; `enforcedBy` names that rule, and the checker
requires one. `format` is the archetype: read with `{}` so an absent token does not
raise inside `std/json`, then refused by name against the readable set.
A member §5 names that this reader does not consume must say who does. Without it the
census would quietly accumulate members nothing reads, which is the other direction of
the same defect and the direction `counts` sat in: §5.2 required it, the reader never
opened it, and the tally's whole stated purpose — 'so a partial ingest is detectable' —
was served by nobody.
── WHY `defaultPath` IS HERE AND NOT IN THE READER ───────────────────────────────────
§5.1's rule is that every path but `snapshot.json` is named by the row that owns it.
FIVE of them carry a default for a capture whose row is silent — the four per-row
sidecars and the one snapshot-wide one — and a row's `container` carries none, because
it is required of every traced row and a row that names none is refused. A default
open-coded in the reader is a convention; a default stated in the contract is part of
the contract. So the reader spells none of the five and takes all five from here, and
`snapshot-contract-selftest.mjs` §8 fails if any of them appears as a path literal in
the reader — which it did, for `sources`, until 2026-09-17.

S5-SNAPSHOT-PRESENT.statement: A snapshot is a directory holding `snapshot.json`; that one file is read by name.

S5-FORMAT-UNKNOWN.statement: A `format` token the reader does not support is refused by name, naming the tokens the build accepts, and nothing is read.

S5-CHAIN-NAMED.statement: `provenance.chain` is required and is never guessed.

S5-CHAIN-UNIQUE.statement: A chain slug another producer already owns is refused at ingest rather than resolved.

S5-MEMBERS-REQUIRED.statement: Every member §5.2's table marks required is present; a snapshot short of one is refused naming the member rather than raising where it is first reached.

S5-ROW-MEMBERS-REQUIRED.statement: Every member §5.2b marks required and reaches by an unguarded subscript is present on the row that must carry it; a row short of one is refused naming the row and the member rather than raising inside the JSON reader.

S5-COUNTS-PRESENT.statement: `counts` is required: a snapshot with no tally has no detector for a partial ingest.

S5-COUNTS-ROWS.statement: `counts.blocks` and `counts.transactions` are measurements of the rows beside them and must equal their lengths.

S5-COUNTS-RECONCILE.statement: On `@2`, `counts.accountedFor` ranges over traced, untraced and chain-absent and equals `counts.transactions`.

S5-RECORDER-LABEL-UNIQUE.statement: Two recorder commits in one snapshot that shorten to one version label are refused; the label is what the build hash is derived from.

S5-CONTAINER-NONEMPTY.statement: A row that names a container must name one with bytes in it.

S5-REASON-REQUIRED.statement: A row that carries no trace carries a `reason`, and an empty reason is refused rather than published.

S5-REFUSALREASON-REQUIRED.statement: On `@2` every untraced row carries a `refusalReason`; a row without one is refused, naming the row.

S5-REFUSALREASON-CLOSED.statement: `refusalReason` is drawn from a closed set; a value outside it is refused rather than carried or dropped.

S5-REFUSALREASON-FORBIDDEN.statement: A chain-absent row carries the sentence and NOT the member; the closed set is a set of things this pipeline did.

S5-BUNDLE-REQUIRED.statement: A recording that claims source level, or that carries positions, is refused without a source bundle beside it.

S5-BUNDLE-KEYED.statement: A source bundle is keyed by contract-class identity; one with no `codeHash` cannot be reached from a manifest.

S5-BUNDLE-NONEMPTY.statement: A source bundle with no files is refused rather than published and then recommended.

S5-INSTRUCTIONS-AGREE.statement: An instruction listing whose step count differs from the recording's is refused at publish time.

S5-POSITIONS-AGREE.statement: A position stream whose step count differs from the recording's is refused at publish time.

S5-POSITIONS-COLUMNS.statement: Every column of a position stream is as long as the recording's step count; a partial column would mark rows it was never measured for.

S5-CALLTRACE-AGREE.statement: A call trace's frame count must be the recording's `callsOpened` plus the synthetic top-level frame.

S5-CALLTRACE-FRAMES.statement: A call trace must carry as many frames as it declares.

S5-CALLTRACE-FOLD-NONEMPTY.statement: A frame marked folded claims something is behind it; folding with zero hidden descendants is refused.

S5-CALLTRACE-FOLD-TALLY.statement: A call trace's fold summary must be the sum its own frames carry.

S5-CALLTRACE-FOLD-BOUND.statement: A call trace may not fold more steps than the recording has.

S5-SIDECAR-FORMAT-UNKNOWN.statement: A sidecar that carries its own version token is refused by name when that token is one the reader does not support.

S5-SIDECAR-CHAIN.statement: A sidecar that names a chain must name this snapshot's; attaching one chain's answers to another's transactions is refused.

format.holds: the version token; §5.2a is the policy

provenance.holds: who produced this, against what, when — including the chain slug

window.holds: the range the producer could reach, as the node answered it

counts.holds: the producer's own tally, so a partial ingest is detectable

transactions.holds: one row per transaction the enumeration saw, traced or not

captures.holds: one entry per catch of a supervised watch, each naming the build that was running

artifactResolution.holds: where the artifact-resolution sidecar is, if this capture has one

chain.holds: the slug the published tree is keyed by

label.holds: the display name a banner shows; the reader supplies a neutral one when absent

runtimeCommit.holds: the chain's DEFAULT recorder commit, for rows that name none of their own

endpoint.holds: the node this capture was taken against, republished verbatim

capturedAt.holds: the instant the capture stopped, republished verbatim

nodeVersion.holds: the node's own version string, republished verbatim

l1ChainId.holds: the settlement chain's id where the chain has one; meaningless on a chain with no L1, and therefore never required

finalized.holds: the node's own finalized tip at capture, which is what the published pointer names

blocks.holds: how many blocks the replay window spans, republished verbatim
the length of `blocks`, derived on every write

transactions.holds: the length of `transactions`, derived on every write

hash.holds: the block's identifier, which its published object is keyed by

parentArchiveRoot.holds: the predecessor link this chain names its parent by; a chain whose predecessor link has another name states it here under this member

timestamp.holds: unix seconds; a block with none contributes nothing to the published coverage span rather than an invented date

runtimeCommit.holds: the recorder build that was running for this catch

blockNumber.holds: the height of the block that settled it

outcome.holds: which of the three populations this row is in — the partition is `snapshot-format.json`'s

revertCode.holds: the chain's own: 0 succeeded, anything else reverted

reason.holds: the producer's own sentence about why this row carries no trace

refusalReason.holds: the machine-readable member from the closed set

container.holds: the snapshot-relative path of this row's recording

containerBytes.holds: the container's size, republished on the overlay row

effects.holds: what the replay reproduced of what the block published

recording.holds: the replay's own measurements of the recording it wrote

recordedBy.holds: this row's own recorder commit, which outranks every other source

transactionFee.holds: the fee the chain charged, as the row's cost vector

sourceBundles.holds: where this row's source bundle is; §5.1's default applies when it is silent

instructions.holds: where this row's instruction listing is; §5.1's default applies when it is silent

positions.holds: where this row's per-step source positions are; §5.1's default applies when it is silent

callTrace.holds: where this row's call frames are; §5.1's default applies when it is silent

artifacts.holds: what the recording resolved per contract; ABSENT and EMPTY are different answers and the tree keeps them apart

bodyRetained.holds: whether the node still served this transaction's body at capture

effectVisible.holds: whether the chain still published this transaction's effects at capture

refusal.holds: the runtime error class behind a `refused` row, kept as evidence in the published summary

matched.holds: how many published effects the replay reproduced

steps.holds: the container's step count, which every per-step sidecar is checked against

callsOpened.holds: frames, excluding the synthetic top-level one

sourceLevel.holds: the runtime's AND over every contract this transaction executed; absence is FALSE and never true by accident

stepsPositioned.holds: how many steps resolved to a source coordinate

declaredRung.holds: the rung the recording declared for itself

contractRungs.holds: the per-contract detail `sourceLevel` was computed from

contractClassId.holds: the class it ran, which a source bundle is keyed by

resolved.holds: whether an artifact was proved for it

corroboration.holds: how many independent distributors served the same debug symbols

_comment: NO `defaultPath`, DELIBERATELY, and this entry is where the reason belongs.
`ct` was recorded here as the container's default until 2026-09-17 and the
reader never used it — it could not: `transactions[].container` is required
of every traced row and taken by an unguarded subscript, so a traced row that
names no container is REFUSED by S5-ROW-MEMBERS-REQUIRED rather than resolved
to anything. A `defaultPath` here therefore stated a fallback that no code
path can reach, and it had to be hand-exempted from the check that every
default belongs to a container the reader opens — a default that is both
unreachable and excused from the arm that would have said so.
`ct/<txId>.ct` is still the layout every producer in this tree writes, and
§5.1's table still shows it. It is a CONVENTION a producer gets for free,
which §5.1 distinguishes from a default: the row names the file, and if the
row is silent the snapshot is non-conforming.

bundles.holds: one entry per contract class whose source text this capture carries

codeHash.holds: the contract class id this bundle is keyed by

files.keys: open — the interned paths, preserved byte-for-byte
files.holds: path to text, with the keys the container asks for

origin.holds: who distributed the artifact this text came from

artifactHash.holds: the chain's commitment to the artifact

debugDigest.holds: a digest over the debug symbols and file map, which the chain does NOT commit to

shape.holds: the artifact's shape, republished beside the text

corroboration.holds: `corroborated` for two independent distributors, `single-distributor` for one

agreeingDistributors.holds: who agreed on the debug symbols; an absent list publishes as the empty one

steps.holds: the listing's own step count, which must equal the recording's
the stream's own step count, which must equal the recording's

paths.holds: the interned paths the columns index

positioned.holds: how many steps this stream placed

artifactRung.holds: the artifact's rung beside the recording's, which can differ

measuredPostHoc.holds: whether these coordinates were computed after the fact; a capture's own stream outranks a reconstruction

frames.holds: the frame count, which must be the recording's `callsOpened` plus one

foldedFrames.holds: how many frames this stream folds

foldedSteps.holds: how many steps sit behind those folds

name.holds: the frame's name, used in a refusal

foldedBy.holds: which fold rule closed this frame

hiddenDescendants.holds: frames behind it; zero on a folded frame is refused

format.holds: this sidecar's OWN version token, separate from the snapshot's

chain.holds: the chain these answers are about; a mismatch is refused

transactions.holds: one entry per transaction answered about

runtimeCommit.holds: the resolver build, republished per transaction

txHash.holds: which transaction this entry answers about

artifacts.holds: the same shape as the row's own `artifacts`; `null` is the tool's 'this run did not finish asking'

positions.holds: the same shape as the positions sidecar; carried forward only when it positioned a step

resolved.holds: whether an artifact was proved for it

paths.holds: the interned paths the columns index

positioned.holds: how many steps this stream placed

_comment: §5.4's boundary, stated as NAMES so the claim is checkable rather than a category:
no snapshot-relative path the reader resolves may be one of these.
TWO OF THE SIX HAVE A PRODUCER IN THIS TREE AND FOUR DO NOT, and saying so is the
point rather than an omission. `tools/chain/ingest-range.mjs` writes a
`blocktracer/coverage-ledger@1` at `<state>/coverage.json` and per-range directories
under `<state>/ranges/` — those two are real, and the byte-identity arm in
`tests/tchainsnapshot.nim` plants both beside a real capture. `cursor.json`, `lease`,
`lease.json` and `.lock` are §5.4's OTHER two categories (cursors and leases) with no
instance in this tree today, so the sweep over them is currently vacuous — it would
still catch a reader that learned to open one, which is what the list is for, but a
green over those four is not evidence about anything that exists. `writtenBy` records
which is which so the next reader does not have to grep for it.
